claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure exhibiting multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A transformer model using chemical-composition and hierarchical-microstructure descriptors can predict Young’s modulus of HfNbTiVAl10.
The same transformer model can predict the yield strength of HfNbTiVAl10.
The same transformer model can predict the fracture toughness of HfNbTiVAl10.
Combining experimental measurements and simulation outputs in the training dataset will enable a single transformer framework to replace the conventional multi-method workflow.
Microstructural heterogeneity and multiscale chemical fluctuations mediate the relationship between model inputs and the mechanical properties of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
Transformer self-attention can capture complex relationships among alloy chemical features.
Transformer self-attention can capture relationships among detailed hierarchical structural features.
Attention allows the model to focus on features governing elastic and plastic behavior.
The learned mapping reduces dependence on computationally expensive physics-based simulations.
Ab initio, molecular-dynamics, and CALPHAD-based approaches can require substantial computational time or resources for HEA prediction.
Existing approaches are particularly limited for predicting fracture-related properties.
The transformer could reduce prediction time by as much as a factor of ten.
The transformer could achieve errors comparable to or lower than CALPHAD and first-principles workflows for Young’s modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness.
Prediction errors may be reduced by approximately 10–15%.
Model reliability will deteriorate if the training data do not span the relevant variation in microstructural heterogeneity.
Model reliability will deteriorate if the input descriptors omit important aspects of the hierarchical structure.
The model may be unreliable for previously unseen structural phenomena outside the training distribution.
The proposed evaluation uses a blinded HfNbTiVAl10 test set and compares transformer predictions and runtime against a conventional CALPHAD/first-principles workflow.
